key_insight: XCAPE combines powder X-ray diffraction constraints with machine-learning-guided crystal structure search to recover physically plausible atomic structures.
engineering_relevance: The framework could help resolve unknown material structures and accelerate automated materials discovery workflows.
method: Constrain a symmetry-aware evolutionary search using composition, unit cell, space group, and PXRD data.
Explore Wyckoff-site configurations through tailored mutations and evaluate energy and diffraction agreement.
Accelerate geometry optimization with a universal machine-learning interatomic potential.
evidence_signal: XCAPE recovered 71/77 benchmark structures (92.2%) from simulated PXRD and 12/12 experimental references; among 12 additional candidate assignments, 10 were within 10 meV/atom of the DFT convex hull.
watch_item: PXRD agreement and energetic competitiveness do not establish a unique structure, so new candidate assignments require independent validation.
paper_title: Physics-Guided Crystal Structure Elucidation from Powder X-Ray Diffraction with Universal Machine-Learning Interatomic Potentials
